mathematical_review: decode_pool uses a rounded candidate followed by exact bitwise re-encoding, so this is strict canonical inversion, not tolerant nearest-value acceptance. For N≤65535, F32 rounding error times N is <0.002, far below half an integer, so the candidate step recovers every valid count.
Exact re-encoding rejects neighboring F32 values and noncanonical negative zero. Fine pooling honors the explicit per-cell compartment map.
Global first difference covers either compartment; KC equality includes that step, rule equality excludes it. No extra delay grace is asserted.
No-divergence remains null with a complete current-bridge observed prefix, while per-cell taught history is explicitly not established.
KC-used vectors are recorded after KC spike injection and before gain update in native RateBridge.interval; their equality through the first divergent pooled-DAN step is appropriate.
The code detects observed prefix contradictions; cell-level equality still requires the independently specified source/mapping assumptions, not just matching aggregate summaries.
